title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages): M is a free Z/4-module of rank 2, i.e. the 4-torsion of an elliptic curve in characteristic ≠ 2. M_0 = M/2M ≅ F_2^2, and J is the set of the three NON-ZERO elements of M_0^*. The octahedron Δ = Δ_M has as vertices the six classes {±ξ} of elements ξ of order 4 in M^*. These are the 6 cusps of X(4), Klein's octahedral picture. The map Δ → J, {±ξ} ↦ ξ mod 2, has fibres of two opposite vertices, so J is the set of the 3 diagonals.

(34) Faces: the set F(Δ) of faces equals the set of 3-element subsets of Δ mapping bijectively to J, i.e. sections of Δ → J. It is a torsor under F_2^J, acting by flipping vertices along diagonals.

(35) Since |J| = 3 is odd, F_2^J splits as V_J(F_2) × F_2. Here V_J(F_2) is the sum-zero hyperplane, identified with M_0 via m ↦ (i(m))_{i∈J}; the F_2 factor is the diagonal. The non-zero diagonal element ε_Δ (flip every vertex) acts on faces as the antipodal map.

(36)-(37) Canonical bijection F(Δ_M) ≅ P_M/ζ, with ζ = {±id_M} the centre of Gl(M). Here P_M = {(ξ_i)_{i∈J} ∈ (M^*)^J : ξ_i lifts i, Σξ_i = 0}. Count check:
- There are 4^3 = 64 lift triples, and the sum condition cuts this to 16.
- Changing the sign of ξ_i changes the sum by 2ξ_i, which corresponds to i. So the sign changes act through the surjection F_2^3 → F_2^2 with kernel the diagonal.
- Hence each face has exactly two sum-zero lifts, differing by −1, and P_M/ζ has 8 elements, as it should.

(38) Comparison of extensions:
- Top row: 1 → (1+2End M)/{±1} ≅ End(M_0)/F_2·id ≅ M_0 × F_2 → Gl(M)' = GL_2(Z/4)/{±1} → GL(M_0) ≅ S_J → 1.
- Bottom row: 1 → F_2^J → Aut_oct(Δ) → S_J → 1, the hyperoctahedral group W(B_3) = (Z/2)^3 ⋊ S_3 ≅ S_4 × C_2 = O_h.
- The vertical maps are isomorphisms, re-proving Gl(M)' ≅ Aut_oct(Δ_M) (order 48), now compatibly with the filtrations.
- From the previous page: the centre F_4/F_2 ⊂ End(M_0)/F_2 corresponds to the antipodism ε_Δ.

End of page: Aut_oct(Δ)_ab ≅ (Aut^+ × {1, ε_Δ})_ab ≅ F_2 × F_2. Its three non-trivial characters will correspond (next page) to three canonical 2-element sets:
- the colourations C_Δ (the two inscribed tetrahedra / face 2-colourings);
- the orientations Or(Δ);
- ω_J (orientations of J).
On the Gl(M) side these are, respectively, sg·det, det and sg, with Or ∧ ω ∧ C trivial. The next page concludes Or(Δ) ≅ μ = [det M]^*. The marginal NB sketches how the data of an (oriented) octahedron is equivalent to a 3-element set I with a 2-fold cover / F_2-structure plus extra data.

Purpose: a canonical, coordinate-free dictionary between level-4 structures (Jacobi/Legendre-type normal forms in char ≠ 2) and the octahedral combinatorics of X(4), including the semilinear (det/μ_4) part of the symmetry.
errors: The transcription's '(J = M_0^*)' should be J = M_0^* minus 0 (the three non-zero elements); with all of M_0^* the counts (S_J ≅ GL_2(F_2) of order 6, 3 diagonals) would fail.

Grothendieck's own notation is loose: 'ξ̇_i = i_*' means ξ_i reduces mod 2 to i; ξ̇ denotes the class {±ξ} ∈ Δ. No mathematical error found: the orders 16/2 = 8 faces and 48 for both groups, and the splitting of F_2^J (since 3 is odd), all check.

ideas.what: Vertices of the octahedron = order-4 elements of M^* modulo ±1 (cusps of X(4)), with diagonals = non-zero elements of M_0^*, and faces = torsor under F_2^J
ideas.modern_name: Klein's octahedral tessellation of X(4); cusps of Γ(4)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions regular polyhedra and modular curves in general terms; this explicit treatment is unpublished

ideas.what: Canonical bijection between the faces of Δ_M and P_M/{±1}, the triples of lifts with sum zero
ideas.modern_name: torsor description of faces / level-4 structure combinatorics

ideas.what: Isomorphism of extensions GL_2(Z/4)/{±1} ≅ (F_2)^3 ⋊ S_3 = W(B_3) ≅ O_h, matching the congruence kernel with F_2^J and the centre with the antipodism

Three non-trivial characters of Aut_oct(Δ) ↔ three canonical 2-element sets (colourations, orientations of Δ, orientations of J), matched with sg·det, det, sg, with orientation of Δ ≅ μ_4-type torsor [det M]^*
ideas.modern_name: canonical torsors attached to the characters; Weil pairing as orientation
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (Weil pairing / Galois action on X(4) over Q(i))

missed.claim: A fully canonical (coordinate-free, torsor-theoretic) dictionary between level-4 structures on M and octahedron data: faces as P_M/ζ, the antipodism as the centre, and the three F_2-characters as canonical 2-element sets. The next page adds Or(Δ) ≅ [det M]^*. This is a careful packaging of classical facts rather than a new theorem.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only marginally: it gives a clean conceptual model of the semilinear O_h-action on X(4) over Z[1/2], with orientation ↔ μ_4 torsor. This could serve expositions of level-4 moduli or of dessins of regular polyhedra, but specialists know the content.

deep.surprise_reason: The content (GL_2(Z/4)/±1 ≅ octahedral group O_h, cusps of X(4) as an octahedron, det as orientation) is classical. The page's value is Grothendieck's canonical torsor bookkeeping, a nice unpublished detail but not a new result.
transcription_corrections: '(J = M_0^*)' should read J = M_0^* minus 0 (the non-zero elements; Grothendieck's superscript is likely a symbol for 'non-zero', not *).
'où ξ̇ = Λ*ξ = 1} ∈ Δ' should read approximately 'où ξ̇ = {±ξ} ∈ Δ pour ξ ∈ M^*'.
'ξ̇_i = i_*' in (37) means ξ_i ≡ i mod 2, i.e. ξ_i lifts i ∈ J.

'à deux éléments remarquables, mentionnés[?] aux trois centres[?] de Aut_oct(Δ)' likely reads '...des ensembles à deux éléments remarquables, correspondant aux trois caractères (non triviaux) de Aut_oct(Δ)'.
In (38) the label over Gl(M_0) is S_J (with F_2 indicating Gl over F_2), and the overbrace on the kernel is M_0 × F_2.
